# EXPANSION CW133-18 — Filled, Not Full

## A prose-first game-content plan grounded in an existing survivor journal entry.

### Prose Wave 133: The Work Between Countdowns

## 1. Expansion thesis

This plan expands attention around filled, not full while leaving the journal row intact. Its center is four people in a room with six chairs. The bank offers different distances and registers for rereading the same recorded material; it does not add a new day, memory, event, relationship, quest, or system.

## 2. Story question

What does it mean for a chapel to fill without becoming full?

## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_38_priest_the_chapel_fills",
  "text": "The chapel filled today. I did not expect it. I have been keeping the chapel for 160 days. Six chairs and a table. For the last 3 weeks, no one came. I sat alone. I said the words I remember. I did not know if I remembered them correctly. Today, 4 people came. The Widow came. The Exhausted Father came. The Historian came. The Child Soldier came. The Child Soldier brought his yellow pencil. He did not write. He held it. The Widow sat in the chair nearest the door. The Exhausted Father sat in the chair nearest the wall. The Historian sat in the middle. I did not ask why they came. I said the words I remember. I said them the way I always say them — not certain I remember them correctly, not certain they are the right words, certain only that they are the words I have. The Child Soldier held his pencil. The Widow folded her hands. The Exhausted Father closed his eyes. The Historian listened. I do not know what the Historian heard. The Historian is the bunker's memory and the memory heard the words I remember and the memory will remember them differently than I said them and that is what memories do. I said the words. Four people came. The chapel filled. It was not full. It was filled. The filling is the thing. The filling is the thing that happened after 3 weeks of empty. I do not know if they will come back. I know they came. The chapel is 6 chairs and a table and 4 people and a yellow pencil and the words I remember. That is enough. It has to be.",
  "timestamp": "Day 203, 19h",
  "author_name": "The Priest",
  "author_id": "the_priest",
  "knowledge_key": "priest_chapel_fills_four_came",
  "day": 203,
  "hour": 19.0
}
```

## 4. Fixed canon and open space

After three weeks with no visitors, four people come to the chapel: the Widow, Exhausted Father, Historian, and Child Soldier. The Child Soldier holds the yellow pencil but does not write; the Priest repeats the words he remembers without certainty about them. The Priest does not know whether they will return. Do not add a reason for attendance or claim the chapel will remain filled. Candidate language may add an image, rhythm, or private impression as an editorial draft, but no proposed addition becomes a further remembered event or confirmed fact until the existing content owner selects and reviews it against the source.

## 5. Human center

The source voice is The Priest. The Priest counts four people, six chairs, a pencil, and remembered words whose correctness remains uncertain. Let the distinction between filled and full stand without making attendance a conversion or a promise. The prose may notice what the author can count, hear, repair, fear, or leave uncertain, while keeping the account’s limits visible.
